messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing missing trace_id on short-lived worker logs? Hard to join logs -> spans for quick 200ms paths. Saw a bunch of request_id but no trace.* fields.

kevin: Yep. Our JS runtime emits `traceparent` header but I suspect some infra (alb/nginx) strips or OTLP log pipeline isn't parsing it. Not seeing it in vector payloads.

ashley: telemetry-bot posted an OTLP exporter rollout yesterday to move logs through otelcol. Could be related. deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-10T14:02 by @kevin -> otelcol/logs v2.1.

sam: Quick thought: we can enrich at ingest (otelcol logprocessor) and synthesize `trace.trace_id` from `traceparent` header if present. Pro: no app changes. Con: if header absent, no recovery.

maria: We also need span_id in some places for per-span drilldowns in Console (flamegraph and per-span metrics). If we only tag trace_id, linking will be fuzzy.

kevin: On the runtime side we can add logger middleware to push `trace.trace_id` and `trace.span_id` into structured logs for Java/Go/Python/Node. Java and Go have auto-instrumentation hooks; JS/py we need owners.

ashley: Also important: cardinality/cost. Adding trace_id as a high-card field on every log increases index/storage costs and query latencies. We should measure. Dashboard idea: show join-rate vs storage delta during rollout.

telemetry-bot: otelcol config note: added `parse_traceparent` processor and `attributes_to_resource` step in staging on 2026-03-09. Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/otel/enrich-logs (internal).

maria: Who decides canonical field name? `trace_id`, `log.trace_id`, `trace.trace_id`, `otel.trace_id` — Console queries currently expect `trace.trace_id` in some widgets. Need a decision to avoid fragmentation.

sam: Proposal: canonicalize on ingest to `trace.trace_id` and keep backwards mappings for `log.trace_id` and `otel.trace_id`. Ingest normalization layer does the mapping so dashboards can assume one name.

kevin: I'll open a PR to the otelcol pipeline to normalize names + add a small processor to copy `traceparent` -> `trace.trace_id`/`trace.span_id`. Also adding an SDK doc for owners to include `traceparent` in structured logs.

ashley: Suggestion for rollout: 1) enable enrich in staging, 2) pick ~10 services (low qps) and enable SDK header-preserve + logger middleware, 3) compare join rate (logs->traces) and storage cost. If join rate delta > 90% we'll widen.

maria: Also add a QA checklist item: for each service, run `curl` traces with `traceparent` header and verify we can query log entries by `trace.trace_id` in Console within 30s.

kevin: Pinging owners: @ashley can you coordinate the dashboard tiles (join-rate, storage-by-tag, avg-query-lat)? I'll draft otelcol PR.

ashley: Yup, will add tiles and a short-runbook for the rollout (including rollback if storage delta > 20%).

maria: One more edge-case: ephemeral functions that call downstream services where trace is started downstream (no incoming traceparent). We might try probabilistic join via request_id mapping but probably out of scope for MVP.

sam: Agree, leave request_id heuristics for phase 2. Phase 1: ensure traceparent preservation + ingest enrichment + SDK middleware.

kevin: ack. Opening PR and adding unit tests for the processor. Will include the sample otelcol snippet in PR: 
```
processors:
  parse_traceparent:
    keep_attributes: true
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: trace.trace_id
        from_attribute: otel.traceparent.traceid
      - key: trace.span_id
        from_attribute: otel.traceparent.spanid
```
ashley: Nice. Add a note about retention-policy impacts to finance (cc: @finance).

telemetry-bot: ticket created: T-4582 "log->trace linking rollout" (owners: kevin, ashley, sam).

maria: Thanks all — let's reconvene after PR and first-stage rollout metrics. :thumbsup:
